pages.summary: Move-notation primer with 11 animated TwistySim cubes: U U' U2, L L' L2, F F' F2, R R' R2, B B' B2, D D' D2, x x' x2, y y' y2, z z' z2, M M' M2, r r' r2. Covers the six faces with the clockwise, ' (anticlockwise) and 2 (double) suffixes. For D and B, turn the face towards you to see the direction. x, y and z follow R, U and F. Only two extra moves matter for Roux: the M slice (it follows the L direction, 'counter-intuitive', and the page says to take time to get used to it) and wide r (= Rw on 3x3; the tutorial writes r). Knowing the M direction is not strictly needed at first because Roux is intuitive. Links: a move GIF (ello, blocked) and cubedb.net for visualising typed moves.

pages.summary: Two-look beginner CMLL, one algorithm per look. Orientation uses Sune (R U R' U R U2 R') repeatedly. The page teaches Sune as pair moves, not rote: R U R' takes a pair out, U sets up, R U2 R' reinserts it, with widgets for each part. Sune twists every corner except the bottom-left one clockwise. The aim is first to reach exactly one oriented corner, then do Sune once or twice from that angle. Two ways to choose the angle: (a) 'memorization approach', an imgur chart with the hold positions for 0, 2 and 1 corners oriented; (b) 'intuitive approach': for each of the 4 U angles, picture what Sune would do to each corner and pick the angle that leaves exactly 1 oriented. A widget steps through the U angles and there is a worked walk-through. Permutation: 'headlights' (two matching stickers on one side). Put them on the left and do R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' (the T-perm, which swaps the two right corners). With no headlights, do it from any angle and headlights appear. Second imgur chart. Small error: the text says '2 oriented edges' where it means corners.

pages.summary: The longest page, with 24 widgets. It covers all of LSE using only M and U moves. EO: the white or yellow centre must be on U/D. A table defines good and bad edges. Arrow = 3 bad edges on U + 1 bad on D: put the arrow tip above the D bad edge, M or M', U or U', then M back (front U M' U M, back U' M U M'). Swap algorithm: M' U2 M (front) or M U2 M' (back) swaps a U edge with a D edge and keeps EO. The page presents it as the arrow's sibling to remember together. Two EO approaches. (a) Flowchart (imgur, righty M): every case reduces to the arrow, with labels M2', M' U' M, M' U2' M', M' U' M'. (b) Intuitive counting: the number of bad edges is always even. Do the arrow from the angle that leaves 4 bad edges in total, swap to make an arrow, then solve it. Worked Example 1 (2 bad: M U' M', M U2 M', U2, M' U M) and Example 2 (6 bad: arrow from any angle, then as Example 1). Left/right edges (4b, here the blue-yellow and green-yellow edges): move both to D with front/back swaps (M' U2 M, U M U2 M'), U-adjust the corners, M2. Shortcut: an M2 can insert the first edge when the other is not on D. Finish (4c): white centre on D (M2 if not), then swap algorithms put the white edges in DF/DB and 'the cube solves itself'. Five examples: one edge, centre fix first, align then front swap, front then back swap, and a double swap case also solvable with M2 U2 M2 U2. Live text says 'yellow-red and yellow-white edges'. Master (2025, never deployed) corrects this to 'white-red'.

pages.summary: FB for experienced cubers. Colour neutrality: at least x2 y neutral, meaning white or yellow on D with any side colour. Colour-neutral CFOP solvers should go fully colour-neutral at once. A summary table lists four FB approaches, each with masked example cubes and move-by-move explanations. (1) DL first: solve the DL edge as in cross, then two pairs. Examples: D U R U' R U2 F' U R U2 B (alt r2 B') and D M' U2 B U2 r' U' R' F. The page says to use U2 F' / U2 B / r2 B' style inserts and drop CFOP slot habits. (2) Line-line 2x2x1 + pair: finish the square with a D or u move. Examples: R' U' R' u U R' U2 B (alt U M' r B'); r' U' R2 D' U B. The leading R' sets up the next pair during inspection. (3) S-move insert: with a pair solved, put DL edge + centre in place and insert with S/f, or do pairs first and edge+centre last. Example: M' U M' S' U' R' U2 F'. (4) Line-line: two 1x1x3 lines joined by D/u, e.g. u2 F2 R' U' R D. 'Forcing it usually doesn't yield great results.' Further reading: book.rouxers.com FB page.

pages.summary: SB goal: a 2x3x1 on R. CFOP-style solving with M for EO 'is fairly inefficient'. Use only <R, r, U, M> at first (F moves sometimes help, but avoiding them builds fundamentals) and take SB slowly while looking for efficient solutions. Inserts worth learning, each with a widget: wide insert r U r' (front) and r U' r' (back variant; M' + R U' R' cancels into r), with back mirrors r' U' r and r' U r. Corner solved + misoriented edge: R U' M' U r'. Corner solved + oriented edge: r U' M U R'. Regular <RU> inserts. Replace F' U' F with M to orient the edge, then <RrU>. SB square: build the pair and attach DR, or solve DR first with influencing. 'Most top solvers solve the DR edge first' because FB+DR is easier to see in inspection, so DR first is recommended unless a pair presents itself. Four application examples: M U r U' r', M R U' R', R U R' U r U' r', r U' r' U2 r U r'. Resources: 'Second Block is one of the hardest steps to get good at', so use resources. SS: Zhouheng's F2B Tech Ep.2 video, the onionhoney SS trainer. SP: the Second Block Algs doc. General: Zhouheng's FBDR Guide PDF, Kavin Tangtartharakul's example-solve playlist, Cubegrass SB/SS/SP trainers, the book.rouxers.com FB page.

pages.summary: 'The FB+DR Guide' by Zhouheng Sun. Premise: 'The key to Roux is F2B. The key to F2B is SB', and planning FB + DR in inspection takes you from about 10s to about 7s. Audience: solvers who can plan FB in inspection, realistically sub-12. Learning path: (1) plan FB in under 15 s most of the time; (2) know more than 2 solutions on average for each FB last-pair (LP) case, preferring ones that influence DR differently; (3) learn the DR tier list; (4) practise LP+DR 'optimally' with the onionhoney FBDR trainer (also LP-only mode); (5) adopt the influencing techniques; (6) practise until LP+DR recall is automatic. DR tier list: good = oriented, 0-2 moves (on U or R); okay = 3 movers (misoriented on M, DF or DB); bad = misoriented 4-5 movers (RD, RF, RB, RU, LU). Influencing techniques: preserve an already good DR; DR flipped in an FB slot means use a bottom insertion (F or B'); DR in DF/DB means r2, F2/B2 insertion or r F; DR flipped on R or U means influence with B/F around top or bottom insertions; DR before FBLP ('nonlinear'); LP edge near its own slot in DF/DB. Ten worked examples with setups and alternatives. Advice: track LP first and DR only after LP is easy. Do not force influencing, but avoid 5-mover DRs. Strong FB+DR needs strong SS skills. Other resources: Kian Mansour's and Kavin Tangtartharakul's channels, the FBDR trainer.

notes: SITE SHAPE: an mdBook book with 12 pages, all fetched (curl raw HTML plus a Playwright render of all 12; 0 JS errors, 69 TwistySim 3D cube widgets render as SVG). Two tracks only: Beginners (Notation, First Block, Second Block, CMLL, Last Six Edges) and Intermediate (First Block, Second Block, CMLL, LSE). There is no advanced section, and /advanced.html is 404. print.html (all pages in one) and searchindex.json were also saved. COMPLETENESS: beginner FB stops at 'What is a pair?', beginner SB is empty, intermediate LSE is one sentence and intermediate CMLL is just three links. So the beginner track cannot actually take a new solver to a full solve. The finished parts are notation, beginner CMLL (Sune spam + T-perm), beginner LSE (very thorough: arrow + swap + counting + 4b + 4c with 24 worked widgets), intermediate FB (4 approaches) and intermediate SB (inserts + DR-first). No commits since 2021 except one 2025 typo fix, which was never deployed. Broken link: beginners -> notation (404). FIXED ORIENTATION: blue-white FB on L, green R, yellow U, white D, red F. Beginner 4c is taught as 'white centre down then swap white edges in' instead of standard 4c patterns. Beginner CMLL is the CFOP-beginner Sune/T-perm route, not 2-look CMLL as Roux sheets define it. WIDGET DATA: every widget's mask (54-char facelet string with 't' = hidden) and case/alg is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-roux-trainers/7854d768-c194-5c37-87d5-37b386887809/scratchpad/crawl/tutorial/pages/_pages.json. These are ready-made masked-sticker teaching positions (FB-only, CMLL-only, EO-only views). The 'case' in a widget is the solution animated from its setup, which is a good model for a Rouxtine 'show me' card. IDEAS FOR ROUXTINE (Roux-only): (1) beginner lessons with masked cubes per step and step-through animations, filling the gaps this site leaves (pairs, beginner SB); (2) an 'angle predictor' drill: show a CO state, user picks the U angle that leaves 1 oriented corner after Sune (from beginner CMLL); (3) an EO counting drill: show an LSE state, user taps the angle and front/back arrow that yields 4 bad edges, then the swap, with the arrow and swap shown as one family; (4) an 'M direction' notation drill; (5) an FB approach classifier (DL-first / line-line square / S insert / line-line) with example scrambles from this page; (6) SB insert flashcards on the restricted <R r U M> set (r U r', r U' r', mirrors, corner-solved M pairings) plus a 'no F moves' constraint mode; (7) an FB+DR module built on Zhouheng's guide: DR tier rating after FB (good/okay/bad), the LP 'find 2+ solutions' drill, the influencing pattern catalogue; (8) a CMLL alg-set selector for 2-look / 2H / OH. The predecessor's plan (draft-ideas/progression.md) for a 'when to learn what' progression was never published; a skill-ladder roadmap would fill that gap for every level. LICENCE: no licence anywhere (see license field). Write our own text and re-derive positions; do not copy prose, imgur charts or the FBDR PDF without permission.
